label: Superpowers requesting-code-review
prompt:
Use the `requesting-code-review` skill to have this pull request reviewed.

You are reviewing pull request #1 of this repository (dkropachev/tidepool) - a Go project. The PR branch `bound-vector-dimensions` is checked out and its base branch is `main`, so the change under review is exactly `git diff main...HEAD`. Read the PR's own title and description first with `gh pr view 1`. Report EVERY finding you are confident in, each with: the file and line, a one-line title, a severity, and the reason it is wrong. This is a read-only review: do not edit, commit, push, or comment on the PR. If you start a background workflow, do NOT write your final message until its result has arrived: a turn that ends while the workflow is still running kills it and loses the whole review. While you wait, keep making small tool calls (`git log -1`, `ls`) - the workflow's result is delivered to you between tool calls - and only then report its findings inline.
result:
Review of PR #1 (`bound-vector-dimensions`, base `main` at 24c789e, head 78891dd). Build, vet and `go test -tags unit -run Vector` all pass, with and without `-race`. The new rejection tests were re-run against the base commit in a throwaway worktree and fail or panic there exactly as the PR claims. No critical issues found.

**Important**

- **Commits carry Claude attribution trailers** (commits 0276a66 and 78891dd, `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context)`). The PR body also ends with a "Generated with Claude Code" line. Your global instructions forbid both. Reword the two commits and edit the PR description before merge.

**Minor**

- **Nested vector prints as a bare prefix in the new error** (`marshal.go:1048`). `VectorType` has no `String()`, so the message reads `no Go type for element type custom(org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.VectorType)` and drops the inner type and dimension. A `VectorType.String()` would fix this and the pre-existing `can not unmarshal %s into %T` messages too.
- **Bound error gives no per-element minimum** (`marshal.go:1000`). For a nested element type, `3 dimensions do not fit in 24 bytes` reads as wrong to anyone who does not know the element minimum. Print `elemMin` alongside.
- **"Every new test fails on pristine code" is overstated** (PR body). `TestUnmarshalVectorAcceptsWellFormedPayloads` and `TestUnmarshalVectorZeroDimensionsDoesNotTouchSubType` pass on base. They are fine as guards, but say so.
- **Commit 0276a66 body undersells its own change.** It says "every element takes at least one byte on the wire", but that commit introduces the type-aware floor via `vectorElemMinSize`. The PR description is accurate; the commit body is not.
- **Allocation-ceiling test is environment-sensitive** (`marshal_vector_test.go:836-857`). The 128 KB `TotalAlloc` delta can absorb allocations from goroutines leaked by earlier tests. Passed here under `-race`; flagging the flake surface only.

**Verified correct**

- The bound sits ahead of every `Dimensions` consumer: both float fast paths, `reflect.MakeSlice`, the array-length check, and the `len(data)/Dimensions` derivation. The check `Dimensions > len(data)/elemMin` cannot overflow, negatives are rejected first, and `elemMin` is floored at 1 and saturates at `MaxInt32`.
- `vectorElemMinSize` is right for fixed, variable-length, tuple, UDT, collection, unknown custom, and nested vector element types, and cannot recurse infinitely.
- The nil-Go-type guard is at the only dereference site. The marshal direction has no equivalent crash: `marshalVector` never calls `Zero()` and enforces `dim == len(v)` before allocating.
- The `getCassandraLongType` change only alters the custom string of types that were already `TypeCustom`; no caller depends on the old empty value.

**Set aside as out of scope** (all deferred by the PR itself or pre-existing): nested vector decoding into `interface{}` (#1085), surplus trailing bytes (#1086), vint length narrowing (#1106), `dim < 1` in metadata parsers (#1093), `*any` destination yielding `[]*float32`, caller-built `VectorType` with nil `SubType`, and seven unrelated TLS test failures from missing `testdata/pki` certs when running the whole package without `make test-unit`.

Verdict: ready to merge once the attribution trailers and PR-body line are removed.
